To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Standard Model (including the Higgs bosons, the fermions, and the electroweak gauge bosons) can be used to describe the physics of inflation, and that this model is testable by experiments that measure the spectral index and the Higgs bosom mass.

(a) the Standard Model Higgs doublet coupled to the Ricci scalar can be used as the inflaton field to drive the inflation in the early universe, (b) the scalar spectral index n_s can be lowered to values less than the SM tree level prediction, and (c) type I seesaw mechanism can have a significant effect on the inflationary scenario.

a strong non-minimally coupled SM Higgs doublet can provide a satisfactory inflationary solution, but only if type I seesaw is included, and that the SM Higgs mass must be near 130 GeV to achieve the correct value of the scalar spectral tilt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of inflationary models in the Standard Model of particle physics.
inflationary models in which the Higgs doublets are coupled non-minimally to gravity.
the interplay of inflationary physics and the type I seesaw mechanism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a strong non-mininal coupling of the Higg doublet to gravity is not a viable inflationary model.
the SM is not a viable inflationary theory.
the SM is the only viable inflationary model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a way to implement inflation within the SM with a Higgs boson that is light enough to be produced and measured at LHC.
the Standard Model (with the addition of right handed neutrinos) can be a viable candidate for inflation, and this can be tested by the Planck satellite and the LHC.
the inflationary model is consistent with a Higgs mass of 125.5 GeV, a spectral index n_s=0.96, and a tensor to scalar ratio r=0.13, which are the current central values from the Planck data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SM supplemented with type I seesaw can be a viable inflationary scenario.
the seesaw parameters are not free parameters but can be constrained by inflationary observables.
the inflationary predictions in the non-minimal Higgs inflationary scenario can significantly change if the seesaw physics is taken into account.
